entities.summary: Johann Christoph von Bartenstein was an Austrian statesman who dominated the foreign policy of the Habsburg monarchy from the early 1730s until 1753. He played a crucial role in the Habsburgs' efforts to maintain their power in the face of rising European rivalries and the growing influence of the Ottoman Empire. Bartenstein's diplomatic efforts were marked by a series of complex alliances and rivalries with other European powers, including the Holy Roman Empire and the Kingdom of Prussia. His tenure was marked by a series of significant events, including the War of the Austrian Succession and the Seven Years' War. As a result of his efforts, the Habsburgs were able to maintain their territorial holdings in Europe, but at great cost in terms of economic and human resources. Bartenstein's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting the tumultuous nature of European politics during this period. He is remembered as a skilled diplomat and strategist, but also as a ruthless pragmatist who was willing to do whatever it took to secure the interests of his masters. Despite his many accomplishments, Bartenstein's reputation has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries, such as Frederick the Great and Maria Theresa. Nevertheless, his contributions to the history of European diplomacy and statecraft are undeniable, and his legacy continues to be felt to this day.
